name: Use a drill correctly
blurb: Matching bit to material, choosing the right speed and clutch setting, and drilling straight — this is the gateway to every other DIY task.
gear: Bit sets for wood, masonry and metal
steps: Learn the controls: chuck, torque clutch, drill versus hammer mode, and the speed gears. Low gear is high torque, high gear is high speed.
Match the bit to the material: brad-point or twist for wood, masonry with hammer mode for brick, HSS with a slow speed for metal.
Mark and centre-punch or pilot the hole so the bit cannot wander.
Drill straight — sight from two angles, or use a guide block. Angled holes are the most common beginner result.
Learn the clutch for driving screws: start low and increase until the screw seats without stripping the head or sinking too deep.
Learn pilot holes and countersinking for clean, split-free screwing into wood.
tips: Let the bit cut. Leaning on it overheats bits and burns wood.
Always check for cables and pipes before drilling into a wall — a detector costs less than an electrician.
Clamp small workpieces. A spinning workpiece is how hands get hurt.
proof: You drill perpendicular holes in wood, metal and masonry, each with the right bit, speed and mode.
